\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{فجأة} (fajʾatan)}{فجأة (fajʾatan)}]{\ar{فجأة} (fajʾatan) — suddenly, all of a sudden}

\label{lesson:AR-C294-fajatan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to announce, then the Arabic for to declare.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{فجأة}}
\textbf{\ar{فجأة}} — \emph{fajʾatan} — \textquotedblleft{}suddenly, all of a sudden\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{انقطعت} \ar{الكهرباء} \ar{فجأة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{inqaṭaʿat al-kahrabāʾ fajʾatan.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Suddenly the electricity went off.
\end{quote}

An adverb with -an, like \ar{غالبا}. It often opens a sentence: \ar{فجأة} \ar{سمعنا} \ar{صوتا}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{فجأة}} (\emph{fajʾatan}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{f-j-ʾ} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to come upon someone unawares\textquotedblright{}. The noun \emph{fajʾa}, \textquotedblleft{}a sudden coming\textquotedblright{}, takes the adverb ending \emph{-an}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fajʾatan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fajʾatan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inqaṭaʿat al-kahrabāʾ fajʾatan.} — Suddenly the electricity went off.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to announce, then the Arabic for to declare, then say \emph{fajʾatan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{فجأة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Suddenly, all of a sudden\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{وقع} (waqaʿa)}{وقع (waqaʿa)}]{\ar{وقع} (waqaʿa) — to take place; to fall}

\label{lesson:AR-C294-waqaa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to declare, then the Arabic for suddenly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{وقع}}
\textbf{\ar{وقع}} — \emph{waqaʿa} — \textquotedblleft{}to take place; to fall\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{وقع} \ar{الحادث} \ar{قرب} \ar{المدرسة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{waqaʿa al-ḥādith qurba al-madrasa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The accident happened near the school.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يقع}, \emph{yaqaʿ}.

Of events: \ar{وقع} \ar{حادث}, an accident happened. Of places, \ar{يقع} means it lies or is located.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{وقع}} (\emph{waqaʿa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{w-q-ʿ} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to fall, to drop down\textquotedblright{}. A thing that falls upon people is a thing that happens, and \emph{wāqiʿ} is \textquotedblleft{}what has fallen out\textquotedblright{}: reality.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{waqaʿa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{waqaʿa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{waqaʿa al-ḥādith qurba al-madrasa.} — The accident happened near the school.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to declare, then the Arabic for suddenly, then say \emph{waqaʿa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{وقع} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To take place; to fall\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{انفجر} (infajara)}{انفجر (infajara)}]{\ar{انفجر} (infajara) — to explode, to burst}

\label{lesson:AR-C294-infajara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for suddenly, then the Arabic for to take place.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{انفجر}}
\textbf{\ar{انفجر}} — \emph{infajara} — \textquotedblleft{}to explode, to burst\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{انفجر} \ar{البالون} \ar{فوق} \ar{رأس} \ar{الطفل}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{infajara al-bālūn fawqa raʾs aṭ-ṭifl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The balloon burst above the child’s head.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{ينفجر}, \emph{yanfajir}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{انفجر}} (\emph{infajara}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{f-j-r} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to cleave, to make water gush out\textquotedblright{}, the root of \emph{fajr}, \textquotedblleft{}dawn\textquotedblright{}. It is Form VII, \textquotedblleft{}to burst open\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{infajara}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{infajara}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{infajara al-bālūn fawqa raʾs aṭ-ṭifl.} — The balloon burst above the child’s head.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for suddenly, then the Arabic for to take place, then say \emph{infajara} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{انفجر} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To explode, to burst\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{في} \ar{البداية} (fī al-bidāya)}{في البداية (fī al-bidāya)}]{\ar{في} \ar{البداية} (fī al-bidāya) — at first, in the beginning}

\label{lesson:AR-C294-fi-al-bidaya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to take place, then the Arabic for to explode.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{في} \ar{البداية}}
\textbf{\ar{في} \ar{البداية}} — \emph{fī al-bidāya} — \textquotedblleft{}at first, in the beginning\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{في} \ar{البداية} \ar{كان} \ar{الطريق} \ar{سهلا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{fī al-bidāya kāna aṭ-ṭarīq sahlan.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
At first the road was easy.
\end{quote}

It opens a story; \ar{ثم} and \ar{بعد} \ar{ذلك} carry it on.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{في} \ar{البداية}} (\emph{fī al-bidāya}) is the preposition \emph{fī}, \textquotedblleft{}in\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{bidāya}, \textquotedblleft{}a beginning\textquotedblright{}, which is built on the native Arabic root \emph{b-d-ʾ}, \textquotedblleft{}to begin\textquotedblright{} (Lane), the root of \emph{badaʾa}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fī al-bidāya}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fī al-bidāya}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fī al-bidāya kāna aṭ-ṭarīq sahlan.} — At first the road was easy.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to take place, then the Arabic for to explode, then say \emph{fī al-bidāya} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{في} \ar{البداية} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}At first, in the beginning\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{في} \ar{تلك} \ar{اللحظة} (fī tilka al-laḥẓa)}{في تلك اللحظة (fī tilka al-laḥẓa)}]{\ar{في} \ar{تلك} \ar{اللحظة} (fī tilka al-laḥẓa) — at that moment}

\label{lesson:AR-C294-fi-tilka-al-lahza}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to explode, then the Arabic for at first.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{في} \ar{تلك} \ar{اللحظة}}
\textbf{\ar{في} \ar{تلك} \ar{اللحظة}} — \emph{fī tilka al-laḥẓa} — \textquotedblleft{}at that moment\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{في} \ar{تلك} \ar{اللحظة} \ar{دخل} \ar{الأستاذ} \ar{الصف}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{fī tilka al-laḥẓa dakhala al-ustādh aṣ-ṣaff.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
At that moment the teacher came into the classroom.
\end{quote}

A story moves on with it: something happens, and in that moment something else begins.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{في} \ar{تلك} \ar{اللحظة}} (\emph{fī tilka al-laḥẓa}) is \textquotedblleft{}in that moment\textquotedblright{}: \emph{tilka} is \textquotedblleft{}that\textquotedblright{} for a feminine noun, and \emph{laḥẓa} is built on the native Arabic root \emph{l-ḥ-ẓ}, \textquotedblleft{}to glance\textquotedblright{} (Lane). A moment is as long as a glance.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fī tilka al-laḥẓa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fī tilka al-laḥẓa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fī tilka al-laḥẓa dakhala al-ustādh aṣ-ṣaff.} — At that moment the teacher came into the classroom.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to explode, then the Arabic for at first, then say \emph{fī tilka al-laḥẓa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{في} \ar{تلك} \ar{اللحظة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}At that moment\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
